clues: This town sits in the Western Cape of South Africa. It lies about sixty five kilometres north of Cape Town.
In the warm, dry summers here, a local bush turns black. That dark turn gave the whole land around it its name.
Its church was the fifth Dutch Reformed one in the Cape. The town then took a new name in 1829, the one it keeps today.
People once came here for a warm spring full of sulphur. They said its water could cure rheumatism, a pain in the joints.
A shopping centre now stands where that famed spring once sat. A small fountain still marks the spot where the spring was.
